input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: Section 21.1 caps each Party at one month of Fees actually paid — far below the fallback floor of 12 months' fees and inside walk-away territory — and "without exception" overrides the Excluded Claims regime in 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside an illusory cap. We re-base the cap in 21.1 to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and delete "without exception" so the existing carve-outs operate. The retained payment carve-out reached only "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", and defined "Fees" (cl. 1.5) excludes taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and any one-time implementation charge, so we widen it to undisputed amounts due under the Agreement while keeping the Customer-favourable "undisputed" qualifier. Section 21.2's mutual damages exclusion already sits at the preferred position and is untouched.

proposal.summary: Re-base the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, remove "without exception", and extend the payment carve-out to all undisputed amounts due.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and deleted "without exception" so the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) sit outside the cap. We also extended the payment carve-out to undisputed amounts due under the Agreement, since defined "Fees" omits taxes, expenses and interest.
